{{nihongo|{{ill|Bōseikyō|ja|倣製鏡|qid=Q130529515}}|仿製鏡}} also known as "倡製鏡" {{ill|Bōseikyō|ja|倣製鏡|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仿製鏡|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q130529515}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=國史大轍典|publisher=吉川廣文館|chapter=倡製鏡|author={{ill|Hatsushige Ōtsuka|ja|大塚初重|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11433969}}}}</ref> refers to {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|qid=Q35197|lt=bronze mirrors}} crafted in regions surrounding {{ill|Mainland China|en|Mainland China|qid=Q19188|lt=continental China}}, modeled after original Han-style mirrors. These types of mirrors are also distributed in regions like the {{ill|Korean Peninsula|ja|朝鮮半島|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q483134}}, {{ill|Central Asia|en|Central Asia|qid=Q27275|lt=Central Asia}}, and {{ill|Vietnam|en|Vietnam|qid=Q881|lt=Vietnam}}, but the majority are produced in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|qid=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago}}.<ref name=":1">{{Kotobank|encyclopedia={{ill|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ar|الموسوعة اليابانية الشاملة (موسوعة نيبونيكا)|be|Энцыклапедыя Ніпоніка|fa|دانشنامه نیپونیکا|fr|Encyclopedia Nipponica|id|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja|日本大百科全書|ka|ენციკლოპედია ნიპონიკა|lt|Encyclopedia Nipponica|pt|Enciclopédia Nipônica|ru|Энциклопедия Ниппоника|uk|Енциклопедія Ніппоніка|zh|日本大百科全書|qid=Q2660112|lt=Nipponica}}|word=倡製鏡}}</ref>
== Overview ==
{{ill|Bōseikyō|ja|倡製鏡}} is a term used for mirrors created in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|qid=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago}} from the late {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|qid=Q207858|lt=Yayoi period}} to the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, distinct from the {{ill|Wa mirrors|ja|和鏡|qid=Q140446073}} made during the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}} and beyond, which were based on Tang and Song mirrors.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite book|title=Revised Edition: World Encyclopedia|year=2007|publisher=Heibonsha|author={{ill|Taku Tanaka|ja|田中璿}}|chapter=Bōseikyō}}</ref> Mirrors imported directly from China are called {{ill|Hakuzaikyō|ja|般載鏡}}, contrasting with Bōseikyō. Unlike Han-style mirrors, Bōseikyō often have deteriorated representations of divine beasts or inscriptions that are merely decorative patterns with no meaning.<ref name=":0" /> The quality of bronze and casting precision is also lower than Han-style mirrors.<ref name=":0" />
In terms of {{ill|bronze object|fa|شیء مفرغی|ja|青銅器|wuu|青铜器|zh|青铜器|zh_yue|青銅器|qid=Q4390114}}, Bōseikyō contains less {{ill|Tin|abstract|Q1096|af|Tin|als|Zinn|am|ቆርቆሮ|an|Estanyo (ელემენტი)|yi|צין|yo|Tánganran|za|Sik|zh|锡|zh_classical|錫|zh_min_nan|Siah|zh_yue|錫|zu|IsiThanambi|qid=Q1096}} and exhibits lower polishing accuracy, resulting in poor quality as mirrors.<ref name=":2" /> However, features like {{ill|Rei-kyō|ja|鈴鏡|qid=Q85884145|lt=suzukagami}} (mirrors with bells) and other practical yet unconventional designs suggest their primary use as sacred objects rather than functional mirrors in ancient {{ill|Wa|ja|倭國}}.<ref name=":1" />
The earliest Bōseikyō crafted in the Yayoi period were based on mirrors from the {{ill|Western Han|cs|Západní Chan|de|Westliche Han-Dynastie|es|Dinastía Han Occidental|fi|Läntinen Han-dynastia|gan|西漢|hak|Sî-Hon|he|שושלת האן המערבית|ja|前漢|km|រាជវង្សហានខាងលិច|ko|전한|nl|Westelijke Han-dynastie|no|Det vestlige Han-dynasti|sv|Västra Han|th|ราชวงศ์ฮั่นตะวันตก|ug|غەربىي خەن سۇلالىسى|uk|Західна Хань|wuu|西汉|zh|西汉|zh_min_nan|Se Hàn|zh_yue|西漢|qid=Q1072949}}, further copied from {{ill|Korean Peninsula mirrors|ja|朝鮮鏡}}.<ref name=":1" /> Known as Yayoi Bōseikyō, small Bōseikyō, or archaic Bōseikyō, they were mainly produced in northern {{ill|Kyushu|en|Kyushu|qid=Q13987|lt=Kyushu}}, with diameters around 7 cm, often featuring faint patterns and being crudely made.<ref name=":2" /> However, Bōseikyō production became more active during the Kofun period.<ref name=":0" /> The relationship between Bōseikyō used as burial accessories in {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} and earlier Yayoi mirrors is unclear. Some mirrors from this period, such as {{ill|Inner Flower Pattern Mirrors|ja|內行花文鏡}} and {{ill|Square-God Mirrors|ja|方格規矩四神鏡}}, closely replicate Chinese designs but may have reversed motifs due to direct impression molding from imported mirrors. This process led to the production of {{ill|Fumigaeshi Mirrors|ja|踏返鏡}}.<ref name=":2" />
Later, Bōseikyō with designs distinct from Chinese prototypes emerged. Examples include:
* {{ill|Beast-Shaped Mirrors|ja|獣形鏡}}, whose imagery does not match any divine beasts from Chinese tradition.
* {{ill|Twisting Pattern Mirrors|ja|捨文鏡}}, which extract and repeat elements like feathers from divine beasts.
* {{ill|Nipple Pattern Mirrors|ja|乳文鏡}} and {{ill|Beaded Pattern Mirrors|ja|珠文鏡}}, featuring large projections (nipples) and small beaded designs, respectively.
* {{ill|Taryū Mirrors|ja|鼗龍鏡}}, not based on recognized divine beasts, suggesting artisans devised these patterns independently.
* {{ill|Straight Arc Pattern Mirrors|ja|直弧文鏡}}, {{ill|House Pattern Mirrors|ja|屋文鏡}}, and {{ill|Hunting Pattern Mirrors|ja|猎午文鏡}}, which exhibit uniquely Japanese iconography.
Mirrors with bells along their perimeters, like {{ill|Rei-kyō|ja|鈴鏡|qid=Q85884145|lt=Suzukagami}}, deviate significantly from traditional Chinese designs.<ref name=":2" />
{{ill|Taku Tanaka|ja|田中璿}} (1977) argued that Bōseikyō featuring unique Japanese motifs were "not mere imitations," leading to a preference for the term {{ill|Wa-made Mirrors|ja|倭製鏡|lt=Wa-produced mirror}} to describe mirrors produced in Japan.<ref>{{Cite book|author={{ill|Jun'ichirō Tsujita|ja|輝田淳一郎}}|title=Ancient History of Mirrors|year=2019|publisher={{ill|Kadokawa Corporation|en|Kadokawa Corporation|qid=Q17224985|lt=KADOKAWA}}|series=Kadokawa Selection|isbn=978-4-04-703663-5|pp=15-17}}</ref>
